title: Developer onboarding hero scripts
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact lab of hero/tagline and subhead variations specifically written for the homepage and product landing experiences that target developer and platform engineer personas. The goal is not cleverness for its own sake — it is to reduce friction in developer evaluation and shorten time-to-first-inference (TTFI) by surfacing the right assurances and next steps.

Context / problem statement:
- We know from onboarding funnels that many engineers bounce after looking at docs or thinking deployment will be heavy.
- Existing homepage language emphasizes economics and reliability, which resonates with platform leads, but early-stage developer signals (quick runs, examples, minimal config) are weaker.
- We need hero variants that explicitly promise a low-friction exploration path while retaining product-level credibility (SLA/scale terminology) for mixed audiences.

Success metrics (how we’ll evaluate):
- Click-through to Quickstart (target lift +12% over baseline).
- Time to first successful API call (TTFI) measured by quickstart completion events (target -25% median).
- New sandbox signups from homepage (target +10%).
- Qualitative: fewer “how do I run this” support tickets in first week.

Testing constraints and audiences:
- Primary: Developers building prototypes and proof-of-concepts.
- Secondary: Platform/infra engineers validating latency/cost claims.
- Run A/B tests on homepage and /docs/quickstart funnel. Randomize by datum and persist to cookie/session to avoid cross-contamination.

Format for each hero variant below: hero line | supporting subhead | micro-CTA (primary) | developer reassurance bullet(s) | why we think it’ll move the needle.

Variant 1 — "Start small, ship fast"
- Hero: Start small, ship fast.
- Subhead: Production-grade inference you can prototype in minutes — no infra setup required.
- CTA: Try the 2-minute Quickstart
- Reassurance bullets:
  1) One-line code example in hero (JS + curl toggle)
  2) Free sandbox with real models and sample dataset
  3) Auto-scaled hosted mode, pin to Dedicated later
- Rationale: Directly addresses the onboarding friction. Developers see that they can get a token/proof in minutes, reducing bounce.

Variant 2 — "Predictable latency, predictable cost" (lean)
- Hero: Predictable latency. Predictable cost.
- Subhead: Developer-friendly APIs with routing and batching tuned for production workloads.
- CTA: See latency & cost examples
- Reassurance bullets:
  1) Example latency stats for small/medium/large prompts
  2) Transparent per-request pricing preview
  3) Option to reserve Dedicated capacity when ready
- Rationale: Speaks to infra/infra-adjacent buyers who will influence procurement while still offering a path for devs.

Variant 3 — "Your model, our serving"
- Hero: Your model, our serving — ship faster with less guesswork.
- Subhead: Bring open models or use Redwood-curated variants with built-in batching, KV caching, and fallbacks.
- CTA: Bring a model in 5 steps
- Reassurance bullets:
  1) Import a Hugging Face model in CLI example
  2) Fallbacks to cheaper variants if capacity constrained
  3) Audit logs and KMS-ready for private deployments
- Rationale: Pitches the hybrid crowd who value model control but want a managed serving plane.

Variant 4 — "From prototype to SLA" (ops-focused)
- Hero: From prototype to SLA — same API, multiple deployment modes.
- Subhead: Local dev -> hosted sandbox -> Dedicated or Private with seamless rollouts.
- CTA: Compare deployment flows
- Reassurance bullets:
  1) Pin a model version, run canaries, automatic fallbacks
  2) Observability: per-route token cost and latency charts
  3) Example policy YAML for routing by latency/cost
- Rationale: Reduces buying friction for enterprise buyers who want a clear migration path.

Microcopy and inline examples (to include in hero area toggles):
- Tiny JS snippet (one-liner) and curl example that actually work in sandbox — put these above the fold so developers can copy/paste quickly.
- Toggle: "Prototype" vs "Production" quick examples showing how little changes in config move you from one to the other.

Hero micro-CTA alternatives (for testing):
- "Try the 2-minute Quickstart"
- "Run a sample request"
- "Import your model"
- "Compare latency profiles"

Supporting microcontent for product pages (embeddings, streaming, rollouts):
- Short lead-ins per product card (20–30 words) that emphasize immediate developer action. Example for embeddings: "Vector search-ready embeddings — run a sample search in 60s, see similarity results on your own data."
- Each product card should have a small example that’s executable in the browser sandbox and a CTA to "Drop your data" or "Try with sample data".

Placement & layout suggestions:
- Above the fold: hero + one-line snippet + primary CTA + secondary link to "Why devs like Redwood" (short bullets).
- Below hero: three quick-start tiles (Prototype, Pin to Dedicated, Import model) with 60–90s estimated time to complete.
- Right rail or sticky: performance/sla quick facts (p95 latency, per-token cost ranges) to reassure buyers scrolling.

A/B test plan (30-day test cadence):
- Cell A: Baseline (current homepage copy).
- Cell B: Variant 1 (Start small, ship fast).
- Cell C: Variant 3 (Your model, our serving).
- Metrics: Quickstart CTR, TTFI median, sandbox signups, bounce rate.
- Minimum detectable effect: design for +8–12% CTR lift with 80% power; estimate sample sizes and run for 30 days.

Notes / risks / open questions:
- Risk: Too many developer promises might undercut enterprise positioning. Solution: use micro-audiences and progressive disclosure — hero for devs, secondary rails for procurement.
- Need legal/finance signoff on any sample pricing shown in hero.
- Engineering: ensure the hero one-line examples remain runnable as we change sandboxes; assign a small watcher to keep examples green (GH issue/monitor).

Next steps / action items:
- PM: pick two hero variants to instrument in the experiment by 2026-03-10 (linked jira GTMP-213).
- Eng/Docs: freeze the 1-line JS + curl snippets and add monitoring for quickstart completion (owner: @Aisha).
- Design: mock hero treatments and tile layouts (deliverables due 2026-03-05).
- Analytics: set events for quickstart click, quickstart completion, sandbox signup.

Appendix: sample one-line snippet (JS) to feature in the hero toggle:
- fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate',{method:'POST',headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer <token>','Content-Type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify({model:'redwood-small',input:'Summarize product onboarding in one sentence'})}).then(r=>r.json()).then(console.log)

End of doc.
